optional_english_cues.text: Here's an NVIDIA earnings draft. Two figures look plausible. Let's check them before publishing.
Muse Spark extracts the claims. Code checks the SEC evidence. Seven pass, two are wrong, and two remain unverifiable.
Click eighteen percent. The draft says year over year, but eighteen percent is quarter-over-quarter growth.
The receipt calculates the year-over-year change: about one hundred and six percent. We can inspect both filed values.
Now click earnings per share. The draft labels two dollars and twenty-two cents as GAAP.
That is the adjusted figure. The GAAP receipt says two dollars and forty-six cents, with the filing attached.
Let's fix both. Muse Wonder proposes numeric edits; code constrains them and verifies the revised draft again.
The original stays on the left. The rechecked version shows exactly which numbers changed.
Each correction keeps its receipt. This is a recorded successful response, replayed through the actual interface, not a live speed test.
All eleven claims are checked again. The two errors are resolved. Guidance still has question marks; a forecast is not a filed fact.
Copy the revised draft with its correction receipts.
A correct number can still arrive too late. Here is a roundup checked as of July twenty-ninth, sixteen hundred UTC.
Microsoft's filing arrived later. These claims are marked not public yet.
Switch to Now and check again. Those two numbers become verifiable. The cutoff follows EDGAR acceptance time.
The same workflow handles a slide. Upload this seeded earnings table and select Check slide. SAM proposes regions; Spark reads the figures.
Click a numbered reading to open its receipt. Both planted errors are caught. Here Spark supplied the region after SAM found none. The image is a claim, not evidence.
Ask for one figure. Spark proposes the lookup; code builds a verified answer. Inspect its SEC footnotes.
NoCap: eleven companies, SEC receipts. Built during this hackathon by Robert Chang. Explore the saved examples.
